body:
### Problem

On a large selection (>100.000 lines), `getregionpos` adds a significant delay. Both Neovim and Vim show a similar, but arguably large delay. For example, on my laptop, every 100.000 lines add roughly 400 ms. This might indicate a performance issue, or perhaps my expectations are simply too high.

My main concern is that `getregionpos` can be used internally in Neovim:

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/d3b4f562a636a7f9df69a18c27d1e0d7bbad22a5/runtime/lua/vim/lsp/buf.lua#L542-L546

From https://github.com/neovim/neovim/discussions/38271#discussioncomment-18121600:
> So, when the goal is simply to select a contiguous visual block based only on the start and end positions, I'd think twice before using it.

> [!NOTE]
> The current `range_from_selection` implementation runs in a fraction of a millisecond on the same file.

| Implementation | Average of 10 (in ms) |
|-|-|
| Neovim `getregionpos` | 348.256894 |
| Vim `getregionpos` | 392.054834 |
| Neovim `range_from_selection` | 0.0330133 |

### Steps to reproduce

```
yes 'local a = 67' | head -n 100000 > large.lua
nvim --noplugin -u repro.lua large.lua
val
<F1>
<F2>
```

```lua
-- repro.lua
vim.o.showmode = false

vim.cmd([[
xnoremap <F1> <Cmd>let s = reltime() \| call getregionpos(getpos('.'), getpos('v')) \| echomsg reltimefloat(reltime(s)) * 1000 .. ' ms'<CR>
]])

-- See https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/211bef231519be3e71adc176b078c0f981e861ae/runtime/lua/vim/lsp/buf.lua#L542-L573
---@param bufnr integer
---@param mode "v"|"V"
---@return table {start={row,col}, end={row,col}} using (1, 0) indexing
local function range_from_selection(bufnr, mode)
  -- TODO: Use `vim.fn.getregionpos()` instead.

  -- [bufnum, lnum, col, off]; both row and column 1-indexed
  local start = vim.fn.getpos("v")
  local end_ = vim.fn.getpos(".")
  local start_row = start[2]
  local start_col = start[3]
  local end_row = end_[2]
  local end_col = end_[3]

  -- A user can start visual selection at the end and move backwards
  -- Normalize the range to start < end
  if start_row == end_row and end_col < start_col then
    end_col, start_col = start_col, end_col --- @type integer, integer
  elseif end_row < start_row then
    start_row, end_row = end_row, start_row --- @type integer, integer
    start_col, end_col = end_col, start_col --- @type integer, integer
  end
  if mode == "V" then
    start_col = 1
    local lines = api.nvim_buf_get_lines(bufnr, end_row - 1, end_row, true)
    end_col = #lines[1]
  end
  return {
    ["start"] = { start_row, start_col - 1 },
    ["end"] = { end_row, end_col - 1 },
  }
end

vim.keymap.set("x", "<F2>", function()
  local s = vim.fn.reltime()
  range_from_selection(0, "v")
  local d = vim.fn.reltimefloat(vim.fn.reltime(s)) * 1000 .. " ms"
  vim.print(d)
end)
```

### Expected behavior

1. Slightly better performance if possible.
2. Change the TODO.

### Nvim version (nvim -v)

NVIM v0.13.0-dev-1391+g1deeff9c38

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

**YES**
VIM - Vi IMproved 9.2 (2026 Feb 14, compiled Jul 24 2026)

### Operating system/version

Arch Btw

### Terminal name/version

alacritty 0.17.0 (94e7c887)

### $TERM environment variable

alacritty

### Installation

build from repo

comment_data.body:
> It takes about x2/x3 as long as a Lua implementation generated by free ChatGPT.

I think `getregionpos()` considers edge cases , that may slow it down. So first question is whether the 2x speedup has equivalent behavior.

But there likely is a way to make it faster for the common case, so worth exploring.

Over 95% of the time spent in `getregionpos()` is in list allocation and manipulation functions.
